author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty named in the request and then carry only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole specialty name, disregarding letter case. The machine-readable form becomes a supported surface (REQ-VET-003).
acceptance_criteria: /vets.html?specialty=<name> renders the directory page carrying only veterinarians holding that specialty, paged as the unfiltered page is
/vets?specialty=<name> returns the machine-readable document carrying only veterinarians holding that specialty
matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case: 'Radiology' matches the stored 'radiology'
a partial specialty name matches no veterinarian: 'rad' returns an empty list, not the radiology veterinarians
a specialty no veterinarian holds returns the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list and HTTP 200
an empty or space-only specialty value behaves as if the parameter were absent, exactly as the empty owner search does
with no specialty parameter, both surfaces behave as they do today: the page pages through every veterinarian, the machine-readable document carries every veterinarian as one whole list
paging links on a filtered directory page carry the same specialty, so page 2 of a filtered listing stays filtered
REQ-VET-003: with no specialty parameter, /vets carries every veterinarian with their specialties, unpaged, as a supported surface
non_goals: no dropdown, form, or other visible control on either surface: the filter is addressed by the request only, and a visible control is a separate request
free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope (NG-9 narrowed, not withdrawn); pet search and visit search stay out
no filtering on any veterinarian attribute other than specialty
no paging added to the machine-readable directory: it stays one whole list
REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn; its identifier is not reused
notes: NG-9 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed-to-allow-specialty-filter.md. One slice covers REQ-VET-004 and REQ-VET-003 because REQ-VET-003 alone is a single characterization test on today's behavior. Narrow readings taken where the request left a choice open, each logged in the PRD Open Questions: a specialty name padded with spaces matches nothing (only blank or space-only text counts as no specialty); a second specialty in one request is undecided; the machine-readable form stays unpaged; no wording is added to either surface to name the active filter or an empty result. PRD edge cases 2 and 3 of the Veterinarian directory section each need a dedicated test.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The mechanism is the project's existing one: a derived Spring Data query on the aggregate's repository, a controller that binds the request and selects the response, and a Thymeleaf template that carries state on its paging links. OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith + OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName + owners/ownersList.html are that pattern end to end, and the vet surfaces mirror it. What is new is the caching boundary: VetRepository's two unfiltered lookups are @Cacheable on an unbounded, never-evicted Caffeine cache, and a filtered lookup would make an unauthenticated caller's string the cache key. That decision is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-lookups.md and stated as current-state rule in docs/system-design.md (new Caching subsection). REQ-VET-003 also retires a Known Defects row: the machine-readable route is a supported surface, not dead code pending removal. Basis for the covering-pattern claims is grep plus direct reads of the named files (IDE oracle not connected in this run).
integration_points: VetRepository gains two lookups mirroring the existing unfiltered pair: a paged one for /vets.html and a whole-collection one for /vets. Derive them from the method name (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) rather than writing @Query; the interface's contract is that its names are Spring Data derivable, and an explicit query here would be the first exception without a reason.

VetController.showVetList takes the specialty as an optional request parameter and threads it into findPaginated; showResourcesVetList takes it and picks between the two repository lookups. Both handlers keep their current shape: bind, delegate, select the response.
vetList.html paging links carry the active specialty. The controller adds it to the model for the template to echo.
No change to Vets, Vet, Specialty, CacheConfiguration, the schemas, or the message bundles. The machine-readable form stays unpaged and unwrapped beyond today's Vets root.

patterns.description: derived paged query taking the caller's search text plus a Pageable; the filtered vet lookup is the same shape with equality-plus-case-fold instead of prefix

controller binds the optional search text, normalizes absent input, and delegates to a private findPaginated helper holding the page size as a local; VetController.showVetList/findPaginated take the same treatment

Web controller row: binds, delegates, selects the response, holds no business rule. Line 91 states the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new rules, so whole-name case-insensitive matching belongs in the query, never in a stream filter over findAll()
no @Cacheable on a lookup whose argument is caller-supplied text while the vets cache is unbounded
case folding is stated in the query, not delegated to the column type or the vendor collation

risks.risk: Copying @Cacheable("vets") onto the filtered lookups to match its neighbours. The vets cache has no size limit and no eviction, and the route is unauthenticated, so every distinct ?specialty= value would mint a permanent entry.
risks.mitigation: The filtered lookups carry no cache annotation. Rule and rationale: docs/system-design.md#caching and docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-lookups.md.

risks.risk: Relying on the database's own case handling. The specialties.name column is plain VARCHAR on H2, TEXT on PostgreSQL, and case-insensitive only by MySQL's default collation, so a collation-dependent match would pass the H2 suite and fail on PostgreSQL - exactly the shape of the recorded REQ-OWN-002 defect.
risks.mitigation: IgnoreCase in the derived name, so the query itself folds case on all three vendors.

risks.risk: Stripping the specialty value before matching, by analogy with OwnerController's lastName.strip(). The PRD's open question settles the narrow reading: only blank or space-only text counts as no specialty, and a padded name matches nothing.
risks.mitigation: Blank check only (null or isBlank selects the unfiltered path); otherwise pass the value verbatim to the repository.

risks.risk: A vet joined twice when two specialty rows differ only by case, or when the join otherwise multiplies rows - duplicate entries in the list and an inflated total element count. The seeded data has three distinct specialties, so no test would catch it.
risks.mitigation: Distinct in the derived name. If the derived count query for the paged form does not come out right, raise a consultation-request rather than reaching for @Query unannounced.

risks.risk: The eager @ManyToMany on Vet.specialties being restricted by the filtering join, so a vet matched on radiology renders only radiology instead of every specialty it holds.
risks.mitigation: Assert in the @DataJpaTest that a vet holding more than one specialty, filtered on one of them, still carries all of them.

risks.risk: Building the paging href by concatenating the specialty into the preprocessed URL literal (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}), which leaves the value un-encoded in the query string.
risks.mitigation: Use Thymeleaf's URL parameter syntax - @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} - so the value is URL-encoded. Confirm the no-specialty case still renders the links the unfiltered page expects.

risks.risk: Proving the matching rules through VetControllerTests, which is a @WebMvcTest over a @MockitoBean VetRepository. A stub returns whatever it is told, so 'Radiology matches radiology' and 'rad matches nothing' would be asserted against the stub, not the query - vacuously green.
risks.mitigation: Matching semantics (whole-name, case fold, unknown specialty, multi-specialty vet) go in ClinicServiceTests, the existing @DataJpaTest with the real VetRepository over seeded H2 data. VetControllerTests keeps what it can genuinely observe: parameter binding, the blank-equals-absent branch, model contents, JSON body, and the specialty on the paging links. testing-principles.md Mocking Policy applies - new tests reach for the real implementation first.

notes: Verdict is new rather than minor because of the caching decision, not the query. Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-lookups.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md); docs/system-design.md gains a Caching subsection and a case-folding paragraph under Persistence, drops the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable route serves no requirement, wires REQ-VET-003 into the Vets/VetRepository/VetController rows, and sharpens Open Question 5 to cover sizing as well as invalidation. REQ-VET-004 joins those three Implements cells when the code lands - a documentation update for the end of the slice, not a design change. No SpecialtyRepository: Vet is the aggregate root and VetRepository is its one gateway, per the one-repository-per-aggregate-root rule. Page size stays a local variable in the controller helper; promoting it to a constant is out of scope here. No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the filtered lookups are Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java:56-84, findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase in Collection and Page forms). Grep of the whole vet package for @Query/createQuery/string concatenation returns nothing; the caller string is bound as a JPA parameter and the case fold is expressed by the IgnoreCase keyword, not by SQL text. Conforms to the SQL-injection row of docs/system-design.md#threat-model.

Reflected output: the specialty reaches HTML only through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (vetList.html:35,41,47,53,59 - @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encode the value, and th:href additionally HTML-escapes the attribute. The slice removed the preprocessed __${...}__ paging literals that were there before, so the filtered surface is strictly safer than the pre-change file. Class sweep across src/main/resources/templates: every remaining __${...}__ occurrence (fragments/selectField.html, fragments/inputField.html, fragments/layout.html, owners/ownerDetails.html, owners/ownersList.html) is pre-existing and preprocesses only template-internal values - fragment parameter names and entity ids/page numbers - never request text. No th:utext anywhere. The value is echoed nowhere else: grep for 'specialty' in templates shows only the paging hrefs and the unrelated vet.specialties loop.

Cache poisoning / unbounded key space: @Cacheable appears exactly twice in VetRepository.java (lines 45 and 55), both on the pre-existing unfiltered findAll methods; neither new method carries it, and there is no class-level annotation. The new methods carry only @Transactional(readOnly = true). No other new code writes caller-supplied text into a cache or into any application-scoped collection. Matches docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-lookups.md and the new system-design Caching section.

Authorization and information disclosure on the reinstated /vets JSON route: no authorization change. The route already existed and was already unauthenticated (docs/system-design.md#security-context records that no authentication, authorization, or CSRF exists anywhere). The change adds one optional @RequestParam and narrows the result set; Vet, Specialty, and Vets are untouched, so no new field leaves the process, and a filtered response is a strict subset of what the unfiltered route already served. Blank input degrades to the pre-existing unfiltered behavior rather than to an error, so no failure text reaches the reader.

Input handling: specialtyAskedFor (VetController.java) maps null and blank to null and otherwise passes the value verbatim to a bound query parameter - no trimming, normalization, or reinterpretation that could smuggle a control character into a different sink. Over-long values are bound as parameters and constrained by the container's request-line limit; the filtered HTML surface stays bounded by the existing page size of 5, and the JSON surface's whole-list shape is unchanged from the findAll it replaces, so the slice adds no new unbounded read path.

Supply chain: the change set touches no build file - no build.gradle, pom.xml, or lockfile in scripts/changeset.sh --name-only - so no dependency, version, or repository coordinate changed and no new transitive surface enters the build. No hardcoded credential, token, key, or connection string appears in the diff; the only credential-shaped prose is the pre-existing security-context description in docs.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix-round delta confirmed to be test- and docs-only: scripts/changeset.sh --base-tree c6ecfa53 (the round-1 review basis) lists exactly docs/system-design.md, src/test/.../service/ClinicServiceTests.java and src/test/.../vet/VetControllerTests.java. No production source, template, or build file changed since the round-1 approval at line 17, so every round-1 security property is verified untouched by construction and re-verified individually below.

Injection: the filtered lookups remain Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java:66-85, findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase in Collection and Page forms). grep -rn for @Query/createQuery/EntityManager across src/main/java returns one pre-existing static @Query in PetTypeRepository and nothing in the vet package; no JPQL or SQL string concatenation anywhere on the specialty path. The caller-supplied specialty reaches the database only as a bound parameter.

Caching: @Cacheable appears exactly twice in src/main/java, both on the pre-existing unfiltered VetRepository.findAll methods (VetRepository.java:45 and :55). The two specialty-filtered methods carry no cache annotation, so unauthenticated caller-supplied text cannot key entries in the unbounded, never-evicted vets cache. The two further @Cacheable hits in the file are Javadoc prose recording that decision.

XSS: the specialty reaches HTML only through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}, at vetList.html:35,41,47,53,59 -- URL-encoded by the link expression and HTML-escaped on output. grep of the whole templates tree for th:utext and for the preprocessed __${...}__ literal finds neither anywhere in vets/vetList.html; the remaining __${}__ hits are pre-existing and in untouched templates (owners/, fragments/), outside this change set. VetControllerTests asserts the encoding positively (page=2&specialty=exotic%20surgery) and negatively (no raw 'specialty=exotic surgery'), so an escaping regression fails the build.

Authorization and information disclosure on /vets: VetController.showResourcesVetList still returns the same Vets projection over the same Vet fields, filtered to a subset. No field, route, mapping, or response type changed in the fix round; the JSON route exposes nothing it did not already expose, and a filter that narrows a public listing discloses no new data.

Supply chain: git status shows no change to build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, or gradle/. No dependency added, removed, or version-bumped by this slice, so no new CVE surface -- dependencyCheckAnalyze not warranted for a test- and docs-only delta.

New test code carries nothing of security concern: fixtures are specialty names and last names only (radiology, RaDiOlOgY, rad, ' radiology ', cardiology, 'exotic surgery'), no credential-shaped value, no @WithMockUser, no security auto-configuration excluded or disabled, no test-scoped property overriding a security setting. The added java.util.List import backs List.of() empty-result stubs.

The two new empty-result web-layer cases mask nothing: each stubs the filtered repository method for a distinct argument and asserts the empty result reaches the model and the JSON body, leaving the existing positive-path and encoding assertions intact. The added ClinicServiceTests padded-name case exercises the real derived query against the real database and pins that a padded name matches no vet, which documents that the controller passes the value verbatim rather than silently trimming it.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Production reach is one package - VetController, VetRepository, vetList.html - plus docs; the row's three modules are one prod package and two test directories, and its oversize trigger counts 6 doc files against 94 prod lines. No config, schema, build, or sensitive path is touched. Both public vet routes gain one optional query parameter and the page's five paging links are rewritten, but the unfiltered rendering is unchanged and pinned by an explicit negative assertion.

semantic_surprise.note: Read all 45 hunks and found no behavior the diff does not announce: the derived findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase carries the case fold in the query name so matching is vendor-independent, Distinct collapses the join for a vet holding two specialties, and the paged count query counts matched vets only (proved at total 2 with page size 1 against real H2). Blank text means no filter while a space-padded name matches nothing and renders an unexplained empty table - user-surprising, but stated in the PRD edge cases and the Javadoc rather than hidden.

test_adequacy.note: The repository tests run against real H2 and assert the actual boundary the code moved - exact match, case-folded match, partial name, space-padded name, unheld specialty, multi-specialty vet, and paged counts - so they would fail against a naive contains-match or a count query that counted join rows. The web tests pin the rendered links both positively and negatively (no raw unencoded value, no specialty parameter on unfiltered links), which is the opposite of tautological; controller-layer stubbing cannot prove matching semantics, but that burden sits at the repository layer where it is met.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers the plan dispatched approved in round 2 with empty findings lists, no escalate tag and no bar_clause; each approval cites verified file-and-line evidence rather than deferring, and the two round-1 changes_requested findings are closed by named tests and a rewritten paragraph. No reviewer in the roster is silent.

scope_deviation.note: The code stayed inside its declared surface with no opportunistic refactor - the cache question was explicitly deferred rather than settled in passing - but the slice carries a product-boundary amendment: non-goal NG-9 is narrowed, the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 route is revived as a supported REQ-VET-003 surface, a Known Defects row is deleted, and four open product questions (padded names, multiple specialties, paging the JSON form, naming the active filter) are settled by narrow-reading defaults with no further owner input. Two design revisions and an aborted autofix-audit round preceded it.

rationale: The code reads clean and the tests pin the real boundary, so the residual is product rather than correctness: this slice narrows a declared non-goal, revives a route the PRD had marked pending removal, and answers four open questions by conservative default.
